title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to Responsible CRM Investments and Skills Development in the Mining Sector in Uganda

description.narrative: Contract related to: Support to Responsible CRM Investments and Skills Development in the Mining Sector in Uganda - This action aims to support the developments in the legal, regulatory and business environment in two of Uganda¿s most strategic value chains, namely: Coffee and Critical Raw Materials (CRM) particularly in post-harvest handling, processing, and aggregation. By optimising productivity, adding value, and boosting climate resilience, it aims to support Uganda¿s economic development by increasing incomes and creating jobs. The initiative will improve the livelihoods of value chain actors by focusing on sustainable productivity, climate resilience, access to finance, and enhanced value addition. It will also promote environmental sustainability, decent work, gender equality, and the active inclusion of women and youth. It will support environmentally and socially responsible investments that advance the shared economic interests of Uganda and Europe. From a European perspective, the goal is to develop Uganda's value chains in compliance with European standards and integrate them with European markets. This action aims to enhance Uganda¿s coffee value chain to boost economic development, increase incomes, deliver sustainable climate smart benefits, as well as creating economic opportunities for youth and women (SO1). It seeks to improve productivity and incomes, climate resilience, and market linkages for 200,000 smallholder farmers through integrated services, including extension, digitalization and facilitating access to finance. The action will enhance seedling supply to ensure climate resilient coffee trees are increasingly grown in the future (output 1.1). It will facilitate investment in the downstream sector to create opportunities for value addition (output 1.2). It will also upgrade post-harvest practices and strengthen rural financial institutions and cooperatives, helping raise income for smallholders, and ensure that Uganda can continue to be a reliable supplier to the EU market (output 1.3). Within the Critical Raw Materials value chain, the EU will support responsible CRM investments, enhance local value addition and promote integration with EU industries (SO2). This includes promoting compliance with EU and international standards and boosting processing capacities. This action will: further provide institutional support to improve Uganda¿s regulatory framework and mining authorities' capacities to provide oversight to the sector including the promotion of transparency, traceability as well as responsible resource management (output 2.1); improve geological intelligence and mapping of mineral resources (output 2.2); support responsible CRM investments that are linked to the EU (output 2.3); and promote artisanal and small-scale mining formalisation with regards to improving regulatory compliance, enhancing sustainable practices and creating decent jobs. (output 2.4). Given the high potential of Uganda¿s mining sector for socio-economic development and the creation of decent jobs as well as the EU¿s objectives to diversify its sources of critical minerals, this action seeks to support the development of an integrated CRM value chain connecting the emerging critical minerals sector in Uganda with European industries, facilitating the preparatory phase of mining and processing projects as well as promoting compliance with international environmental, social and governance (ESG) standards. By supporting key institutions, improving resource intelligence and management, optimising productivity, supporting value addition and responsible investments, required skills development and boosting climate resilience, this action aims to support Uganda¿s socio-economic development by increasing incomes and creating decent jobs.
